findings.where: Article specimen, desktop and phone: the body paragraphs, the subhead 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?', the three-item numbered list and the closing paragraph
findings.fault: The article's running text is centred. Every line starts at a different place, so the eye has to hunt for the next line. In the numbered list the numbers stay at the left edge while each item's text floats in the middle, with lines of very different lengths, so the numbers seem cut off from their items. The title, byline and caption above it are set flush left, so the article starts one way and then switches.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank reader working through Mark's long-form article. The brief calls this the product ('depth after the first look'). Centred paragraphs are slow and tiring to read, and the floating list reads as a mistake. Angélique would also carry this setting into every article she adds.

findings.where: Specimen section labels: 'PALETTE' (blue, tracked capitals), 'Type pair', 'An article page' and 'Motion sketch' (small bold sans), 'Texture' (large italic serif)
findings.fault: Five labels at the same level of the page are set three ways. One is blue spaced capitals, three are small bold sans in sentence case, and one is a large italic serif heading. The blue spaced capitals break the page's own stated rule, 'Sentence case, never tracked capitals'. The italic 'Texture' outranks the sections around it, though it is no more important than they are.
findings.who_objects: The founder, judging whether the type system holds together, and anyone who builds from this tile. The specimen claims a rule that its first label breaks, and the uneven labels make the sections look as if they have different ranks.

findings.fault: The label is set in the link blue but cannot be clicked (the parts map lists it as static, with a link's colour). The page's own note says 'blue only where something can be clicked'.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who reads blue as a link and clicks a label that does nothing. The text-presentation rule says a colour that marks links never colours text that isn't a link.

findings.where: Display serif lines: 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform', the article title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law', and 'Mark's voice…' in the Newsreader specimen
findings.fault: These large serif lines use straight typewriter apostrophes, while the article body and the PDF title use curly quotes and apostrophes. At display size the straight mark stands out and looks unfinished.
findings.who_objects: A careful reader and the founder, who asked for refined, serious type in the manner of a legal journal. A straight apostrophe in a large heading looks like a typing slip, and the mix shows the same mark set two ways.

findings.where: Article specimen header: the title and the byline 'Mark M. Moseley · Blog No. 8 · 18 September 2024'
findings.fault: The byline sits almost touching the last line of the two-line title, with less space than the title's own line gap. The gap after the byline is several times larger. The byline seems to belong to the title's last line, not to the article.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning for who wrote the article and when. The cramped byline is hard to pick out, and the uneven spacing goes against the even rhythm the specimen says it keeps.
